name: Siroi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: Stress is grammatically predictable and is not written. Primary stress occurs on the stem, and if there is a multi-syllable stem, on its second syllable. Reduplicated stems take this stress on the repetition. There are a few exceptions to this rule which are as follows: (1) Compound words take primary stress on the initial root. (2) Pronouns and the irregular verb [...] 'give' take primary stress…

audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (peninitial within the STEM domain, keep dom flag) — or 'morphological' if the catalog reserves fixed-* for purely phonological word-edge rules; 'strict' is not supported by Wells p.5
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim at Wells 1979 p.5 §0.2 in the PDF we hold (p.13). (2) Source: the deciding work is the standard and only reference grammar of Siroi (PL B-51, 1979, vii+218 pp), held in full; Glottolog 5.1 and local indices show no later phonology, instrumental study or OPD, so it is the best available description; StressTyp2 and Gordon 2002 are downstream of the same paragraph. (3) list of works to obtain is short and low-priority (van Kleef 2007 SIL dictionary; nothing downloaded. (4) The sourcing is solid but the classification 'fixed-strict' with word rule 01/010/0100.. overstates what Wells says.
